technical_and_design_decisions: The implementation will be based on the existing Spring XD (now part of Spring Cloud Data Flow) codebase, extending its stream lifecycle management.
Message bus cleanup (U1, U2) will leverage Spring Cloud Stream's binding lifecycle callbacks to destroy associated queues/topics when a stream is destroyed.
For editing deployed/undeployed streams (U3), we will use a state machine approach to allow property updates without full redeployment, using the existing deployment properties mechanism.
Including deployment manifest from file (U4) will be implemented by adding a --properties-file option to the stream deploy command, parsing the file and merging with inline properties.
Reference architectures (U5) will be created as documentation and example projects, not as code changes to the framework itself.
Trace inline deployment properties (U6) will use Spring Integration's wiretap mechanism with global channel interceptors, enabled via deployment property patterns.
Arbitrary side channels (U7) will be implemented by extending the module channel creation logic to support additional named channels beyond input/output, configurable via deployment properties.
The taxi trips study (U8) is a separate evaluation task requiring data ingestion, stream processing implementation, and analysis; it will be delivered as a reference application and report.
assumptions: The development team consists of a single developer with expert-level knowledge of Spring Framework, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring XD.
The existing Spring XD codebase is available and compilable with Java 17+.
All user stories are prioritized and will be implemented sequentially; no dependencies between stories except where noted.
Testing includes unit and integration tests for new features; automated CI/CD pipeline exists.
Documentation (user guides, API docs) is part of each feature delivery.
The taxi trips study (U8) includes acquiring the dataset, setting up a local environment, and producing a prototype with analysis results.
Effort estimates assume a standard 8-hour workday with no interruptions.

activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, clarify vague points, design high-level architecture for the increment, and plan implementation order.
Implement automatic cleanup of queues/topics when a stream is destroyed, including both coupled resources and stale resources from previous lifecycle events.
Add ability to update deployment properties of a stream without destroying it, modifying the deploy/undeploy state machine and property parsing.
Add support for specifying deployment properties via a file (e.g., YAML or properties) and merging with inline properties.
Research and document reference architectures for common use cases using Spring XD, produce example configurations and best practices.
Implement optional trace property for modules using wildcard or specific patterns, enabling wiretap logging/notifications for selected modules.
Extend module channel creation to support additional output/input channels (side channels) beyond primary stream channels, configurable via deployment properties.

activities.activity_name: Study Taxi Trips for Real-time Analytics (U8)
activities.activity_description: Acquire NYC taxi trip dataset, design and implement event-based stream processing pipeline using Spring XD, evaluate performance, and produce a report and prototype.
Run full integration tests across all new features, fix bugs, ensure backward compatibility, and perform system-level validation.
Update user documentation, API docs, release notes, and prepare deployment artifacts for the increment.
